text:
Sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons: HR@10 against 99 negatives measures a different task from full-catalog ranking. RecSys 2025’s [sampling-reliability study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) distinguishes resolution, fidelity, robustness and predictive power; sample composition and exposure bias matter alongside sample size. Earlier [sequential-recommendation experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045) found ranking disagreements under both uniform and popularity sampling. Keep pinned macro validation HR@10 as the selection objective; use full-catalog disagreement as a diagnostic, without substituting evaluators.

For uncertainty, recommended adaptation: retain per-user hit indicators, bootstrap users within each category using identical resampled indices across compared models, then average the four category differences equally. Report the paired macro difference and its confidence interval. [SciPy’s bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) supports paired resampling. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models; they do not capture training variability or repeated-search selection bias. Predefine training-history-length and training-item-popularity slices, report sample counts, and avoid strong conclusions from sparse groups. A [2024 popularity-bias survey](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11257-024-09406-0) documents uneven accuracy across user and item groups.

Proposed diagnostic validation: progressively truncate/shuffle histories, perturb scores, and mix predictions with popularity or random controls. Measure actual pinned HR@10 changes; history shuffling need not degrade every dataset. Across baseline variants and ablations, test whether diagnostics predict held-out control differences beyond popularity and history length. Treat this as an experimental protocol, not an established guarantee. Feedback from twenty training users is exploratory case evidence; it cannot establish population reliability, simulator-trait validity, or validation improvement.
